Compare mp to data book values.

Multiple spots in chromatogram = mixture.

mcqs.q: Why use pencil for the baseline?
What is the difference between a strong acid and a concentrated acid?
options: A strong acid fully dissociates in water; a concentrated acid has a high amount of acid per volume — these are independent properties.
Strong and concentrated mean the same thing for acids.
A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.

mcqs.q: At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.
Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.

mcqs.q: What kind of bond forms between a ligand and a central metal ion in a complex?
options: A strong acid is one that has been heated to higher temperature.
The ligand shares electrons equally with the metal as a normal covalent bond.
A dative (coordinate) covalent bond — the ligand donates a lone pair into an empty orbital on the metal.
The ligand forms an ionic bond with the metal because the metal is positively charged.
